issues.description: Class name mismatch: in the template header (template_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp, lines 30-38) the class is declared as 'Image24' but the constructor and destructor declarations inside that header are named 'Bitmap24'. The template implementation (template_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp, lines 26-31) defines methods for 'Bitmap24' (e.g. Bitmap24::Bitmap24). The solution repository consistently declares and implements 'Bitmap24' (solution_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp, lines 30-38). This mismatch (header declares Image24 while implementation and constructor names use Bitmap24) will cause compilation errors and confuse students about which class name to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class identifier consistent. Recommended: in template_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp rename the class declaration from 'Image24' to 'Bitmap24' and ensure the constructor/destructor declarations use 'Bitmap24' as the class name. Alternatively, change the implementation to use 'Image24' everywhere, but aligning the template header to 'Bitmap24' (as in the solution) is preferred to avoid student confusion and compilation failures.
